messages.content:
You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE TV_Channel (
    id TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    series_name TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    Language TEXT,
    Content TEXT,
    Pixel_aspect_ratio_PAR TEXT,
    Hight_definition_TV TEXT,
    Pay_per_view_PPV TEXT,
    Package_Option TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE TV_series (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Episode TEXT,
    Air_Date TEXT,
    Rating TEXT,
    Share REAL,
    18_49_Rating_Share TEXT,
    Viewers_m TEXT,
    Weekly_Rank REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

CREATE TABLE Cartoon (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Title TEXT,
    Directed_by TEXT,
    Written_by TEXT,
    Original_air_date TEXT,
    Production_code REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT ch.id,
       ch.series_name
FROM TV_Channel AS ch
JOIN Cartoon AS c
  ON c.Channel = ch.id
ORDER BY ch.series_name, ch.id;
```
you gotta check which countries these channels are from

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
       ch.Country,
       ch.id AS channel_id,
       ch.series_name AS channel_name
FROM TV_Channel AS ch
JOIN Cartoon AS c
  ON c.Channel = ch.id
ORDER BY ch.Country, ch.series_name, ch.id;
```
we also need to check if these channels are currently airing the cartoons you mentioned

To check whether they’re **currently airing**, I need a “current schedule” field (e.g., start/end time, currently_airing flag). In this schema, `Cartoon` only has `Original_air_date` (first-ever air date), not whether it’s airing now.

If you want “currently airing” to mean **airing today**, we can approximate using `Original_air_date`:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
       ch.Country,
       ch.id AS channel_id,
       ch.series_name AS channel_name,
       c.Title,
       c.Original_air_date
FROM TV_Channel AS ch
JOIN Cartoon AS c
  ON c.Channel = ch.id
WHERE date(c.Original_air_date) = date('now')
ORDER BY ch.Country, ch.series_name, c.Title;
```

Tell me what “currently airing” should mean for you (airing right now vs airing this week vs still in rotation), and whether you have a schedule table/columns not shown here.
also need to ensure the cartoons are written by Todd Casey.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
       ch.Country,
       ch.id   AS channel_id,
       ch.series_name AS channel_name,
       c.Title,
       c.Original_air_date
FROM TV_Channel AS ch
JOIN Cartoon AS c
  ON c.Channel = ch.id
WHERE c.Written_by = 'Todd Casey'
  AND date(c.Original_air_date) = date('now')   -- remove/adjust if "currently airing" means something else
ORDER BY ch.Country, ch.series_name, c.Title;
```
